key_drivers: Generic congressional ballot polling showing Democrats leading by ~6-7.5 percentage points (Silver Bulletin D+7.6, RCP D+5.7)
Prediction market consensus (Polymarket ~88.5% and Kalshi) indicating a strong Democratic advantage to flip House control
Historical midterm dynamics where the president's party typically loses seats, constrained by polarization and a limited number of tossup districts (~30-40 competitive seats)
Narrow starting Republican majority baseline (~220 seats) from the 2024 elections
args.reasoning: I anchored on historical midterm base rates for the president's party (average loss of ~26 seats post-WWII), adjusted for modern high polarization and fewer crossover/split-ticket seats. Starting from the post-2024 Republican baseline of approximately 220 seats, current evidence shows generic congressional ballot polling averaging D+6 to D+7.6 and prediction markets giving Democrats an ~88-89% chance to take the majority (<218 seats). The distribution places peak mass on a net GOP loss of 11 to 20 seats (200-209 bucket at 36%), with substantial probability on a narrower loss (210-217 at 24%) and a larger wave (190-199 at 21%), while reserving ~12% total probability across majority-retaining outcomes (>=218 seats).
